The Siege of Lachish

Sennacherib besieged the Judean city of Lachish in 701 BC, and the event is commemorated in a monumental series of stone reliefs once displayed in his palace at Nineveh. The reliefs show the assault in remarkable detail.

The reliefs depict an Assyrian siege ramp piled against the city walls, battering rams advancing up the slope, archers and slingers providing covering fire, and defenders hurling torches from the battlements above the gate.

After the city fell, the reliefs portray the captives being led away with their belongings, while the Assyrian king sits enthroned in review of the spoil. Excavations at Tel Lachish have confirmed the siege ramp and a destruction layer from this period.

The panels were excavated by Austen Henry Layard in the 1840s and are now held by the British Museum, where they remain one of the most important sources for understanding ancient Near Eastern warfare and the background of the biblical account.
